The statement signals a sharp negative demand and credit shock from COVID-19, but the FOMC’s rapid move to the effective lower bound and large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repo operations, discount-window easing, regulatory capital/liquidity relief, and coordinated dollar swap lines align with the New Keynesian/Taylor-principle prescription to ease aggressively when inflation is below target and activity weak, and with the liquidity-trap literature emphasizing balance-sheet tools at the zero lower bound. Credit-channel evidence (Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Oliner and Rudebusch) suggests these actions should compress external finance premia and limit amplification of the downturn. With market-based inflation compensation down but survey-based long-run expectations little changed, the Svensson-style inflation-forecast-targeting perspective indicates credibility remains intact, creating room to ease. Net assessment: still negative near term given the pandemic shock and stress in energy/exports, but policy materially mitigates the downside versus inaction.
